title: Default run is low-effort review-only; fix:true has never been exercised
detail: All 6 orchestrator runs used effort:low + fix:false + lanes:[review,schema] + objective:runtime. No run ever invoked the medium-effort fix path, so the fix/downgrade-on-dirty-tree and 429 behaviors are unverified in this history.

title: openIssues trend is non-monotone: 11->14->12->1->0->21 across runs
detail: openIssues went 11,14,12,1,0,21. The steep 12->1->0 drop on 06-16 means accumulated review findings get cleared (likely manual or a fix lane outside this history), not by review-only runs themselves. The 0->21 spike on 06-18 confirms the baseline is fragile and code churn refills the queue. Treat a 0 as 'queue drained', not 'nothing to find'.

title: schema runtime lane reports ~5 findings on non-clean runs; returned null on 2026-06-18
detail: 4 of 5 prior runs report exactly 5 runtimeFindings (first run had 8 + 2 errors). On 2026-06-18 the schema field is null despite schema being listed in lanes — the lane may have silently errored. The runtime lane (buildCliArgs->run.py boundary) is the most consistently productive lane but can return null. Check schemaHistory path when schema=null.

title: runtimeErrors only appeared in the first run (2); zero since
detail: First run had 2 runtimeErrors + 8 runtimeFindings; all subsequent runs have 0 errors. Either the boundary stabilized or earlier runs' findings were resolved out-of-band. Don't assume errors are gone — re-run objective:runtime after any CLI change.

title: coverageDelta is NaN on every run — coverage lane never runs under objective:runtime
detail: All 5 runs set objective:runtime (default), so coverageDelta reports 'NaN' every time. To get a real coverage trend you must pass objective:coverage|both|all; the default lane produces no coverage signal.

title: driftRemaining is 0 on all runs — GUI<->run.py flags stay aligned
detail: driftRemaining=0 across all 5 runs. Either drift is genuinely clean or check:schema was already applied earlier. Drift lane is currently a low-value no-op; budget agent time on the runtime lane instead.

title: Verified review findings skew medium/low-severity; critical is rare
detail: Across non-clean runs severities: 1 critical (once), ~4-5 high, ~11-12 medium, ~4-19 low. 2026-06-18 run: high=5, medium=12, low=4, critical=0. Most verified findings are low/medium. Set fix:true only if you want the long tail; high/critical alone rarely justify a fix run.

title: review-only runs report findings but don't fix them; openIssues only drops via external action
detail: Every run has fix.mode='review-only' (fix:false). The 11->1->0 openIssues drop between 06-15 and 06-16 happened WITHOUT any fix:true run in this history — meaning the backlog was cleared outside the orchestrator. The 0->21 spike on 06-18 confirms the queue refills as code changes. A clean review-only run is not evidence the code is clean, only that nothing new was flagged.

title: delta_from_last is null on every run — inter-run delta tracking is not wired
detail: signals.delta_from_last is null in all 5 runs, so you cannot read 'better/worse than last run' from the envelope. Compute deltas yourself from openIssues/verified/runtimeFindings across history files.

title: Orchestrator completes with empty phases_failed on every run
detail: status='complete' and phases_failed=[] on all 5 runs, even the one that surfaced 2 runtimeErrors. Don't treat 'complete' as 'no problems' — phase success only means the lane ran, not that the code is healthy. Read result.review/schema for actual signal.

title: dirtyTree=false on all runs — the dirty-tree fix downgrade is unverified
detail: dirtyTree was false in all 5 runs (all review-only), so the 'fix:true gets downgraded to review-only on a dirty git tree' guard has never actually fired here. Don't rely on history to confirm that guard works; test it deliberately before trusting it.

title: Clean baseline (2026-06-16) was broken by 2026-06-18 run returning 21 findings
detail: The 2026-06-16 clean run (openIssues=0) was established as baseline, but the 2026-06-18 run returned openIssues=21 — the highest count in history. Code churn between 06-16 and 06-18 (git status shows M python/mlx-movie-director files, M .claude/workflows/gui-movie-director-self-improve.js, new LoRA directory) is the likely driver. Re-establish the baseline only after a fix:true run clears the queue.

title: verified == newFindings on every run — no carryover/recheck of prior issues
detail: In all 6 runs result.review.verified equals result.review.newFindings (each run only reports freshly-detected issues, never re-checks the prior backlog). openIssues is a count of NEW findings, not a persistent tracker — so a downward trend means fewer new bugs, not that old ones were fixed by this workflow.

title: schema lane can silently return null even when listed in lanes
detail: On 2026-06-18 the schema result field is null despite schema being listed in lanes:[review,schema]. First occurrence of null schema result. The schemaHistory path (gui-movie-director-schema-self-improve/iterations.jsonl) is the authoritative log; null result does not mean the lane was skipped cleanly — it may have errored internally. Always check schemaHistory when schema=null.

title: 21-finding spike on 2026-06-18 is the largest single-run count in history
detail: The 2026-06-18 run produced 21 new findings (high=5, medium=12, low=4) — the largest count across all 6 runs and the first >14. This spike followed the clean 0-finding run two days prior and correlates with git status showing M python/mlx-movie-director files, M .claude/workflows/gui-movie-director-self-improve.js, and a new LoRA directory. Code churn in the 06-16 to 06-18 window is the likely driver.
